conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Imposed pursuant to the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above. For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: External walls and roofs materials approval
conditions.text: Construction of external walls and roofs (including dormers) to any building subject of this permission shall not take place until details and samples of all external walling and roofing materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Samples shall be made available on site prior to the commencement of building works, for inspection by the Local Planning Authority which shall be notified in writing of their availability. The building works shall be constructed from the materials thereby approved. In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Vehicle and parking areas to be surfaced and drained
conditions.text: Development shall not be occupied until all areas shown on the approved plans to be used by vehicles, including roads, footpaths, cycle tracks, loading and servicing areas and vehicle parking space have been fully laid out, surfaced and drained such that loose materials and surface water does not discharge or transfer onto the highway. These areas shall not be used for any other purpose thereafter. To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Bin stores and waste storage provision
conditions.text: The approved details for the provision of bin stores (including siting, materials and means of enclosure) and (where applicable) storage of wastes and access for their collection shall be implemented in full before the use commences and shall be retained thereafter as such for the lifetime of the development. In the interests of amenity and to ensure adequate measures for the storage and collection of wastes are put in place.

conditions.summary: Cycle and motorcycle parking provision
conditions.text: Development shall not be occupied until the approved cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities have been provided. The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development. In the interests of highway safety and promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Vehicular access provision and retention
conditions.text: Means of vehicular access to and from the site shall only be as shown on the approved plan 387/03 Rev. A; and delivered prior to first occupation and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the proposed development. To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Phase II Site Investigation and Remediation Strategy
conditions.text: The approved Phase I Desk Study report indicates that a Phase II Site Investigation is necessary, and therefore development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase II Site Investigation Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase II Report and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

conditions.summary: Remediation procedures and unexpected contamination protocol
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

conditions.summary: Remediation works and verification reports
conditions.text: Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Hard and soft landscaping details and implementation
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until full details of both hard and soft landscape works, including a dated implementation programme (inclusive of any phasing), have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Hard landscape works shall include (a) boundary details, means of enclosure and retaining structures, (b) hard surfacing areas, Soft landscape works shall include (c) planting plans (display existing trees with Root Protection Areas (RPAs) and all other retained vegetation), (d) written specifications (including soil depths, cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment) and (e) schedules of plants noting species, planting sizes, root packaging and proposed numbers/densities, (f) drainage proposals. All hard and soft landscaping works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details, approved implementation programme, British Standard BS 4428:1989 and in accordance with Leeds City Council website landscape guidance under 'Landscape Planning and Development'.

conditions.summary: Stone wall retention and maintenance
conditions.text: The stone wall, along the site frontage of St Pauls Street and along the west boundary nearest the access point, shall be retained and maintained, as is, for the lifetime of the development. In the interest of visual amenity and preservation of the historic environment.

conditions.summary: Window design to match existing windows
conditions.text: The design of new windows shall match the style, materials and colour of the existing windows and be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development. In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Commencement of development within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Imposed pursuant to the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above. For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: Highway condition survey and remedial works
conditions.text: The development shall not commence until a condition survey of Main Street and South Approach has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. A plan showing the surveyed areas shall also accompany the survey report. Periodic surveys shall also be undertaken every 3 months and then upon completion of the development (completion of the final approved building on the site) a further condition survey shall be carried out and submitted to the Local Planning Authority together with a schedule of remedial works to rectify damage to the highway identified between the two surveys as a result of the development. The approved mitigation works shall be fully implemented within 3 months of the remedial works being agreed with the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Construction Traffic Management Plan
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a Construction Traffic Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Construction Traffic Management Plan shall include full details of: a) The construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles. b) Proposed traffic management measures on the routes (including South Approach) to site for construction traffic including temporary speed limits, suitable temporary signage and road markings. c) Banned vehicle routing (i.e. left turn out of South Approach/Main Street junction towards Aberford and banned movements during special events (i.e. Leeds Festival).

conditions.summary: Decommissioning Management Plan
conditions.text: Decommissioning shall not commence until a Decommissioning Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Decommissioning Management Plan shall include full details of: a) The vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. b) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. c) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during decommissioning.

conditions.summary: Access sightlines and visibility splays
conditions.text: The access hereby approved shall not be brought into use until works have been undertaken to provide the sightlines / visibility splays shown on the approved plan ref SYS_VS_001 (included as Appendix B of the Response to Highways Consultation Comments); to an adoptable standard. These sightlines / visibility splays shall be retained clear of all obstruction to visibility greater than 0.6m in height above the adjoining carriageway for the lifetime of the development. To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Construction working hours
conditions.text: Construction works, including deliveries, shall take place only between: 07:00 to 19:00 Monday to Friday; 08:00 to 16:00 Saturday; with no works on Sundays or Bank Holidays. To safeguard residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan compliance
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan (ref: AWA7449AMS) prepared by AWA Tree Consultants. To safeguard retained trees and woodland.

conditions.summary: Vegetation protection measures and installation of fencing
conditions.text: No works shall commence until the measures to protect existing vegetation as set out in the approved Arboricultural Method Statement (ref: AWA7449AMS - prepared by AWA Tree Consultants) are in place, including the installation of all protection fencing and ground protection measures as specified by the AMS. The protection measures shall be retained for the entirety of the construction phase with exclusion zones enforced to ensure no equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area nor shall any ground levels within these zones be altered, nor any excavations undertaken including the provision of any underground services.

conditions.summary: Arboricultural supervision of Root Protection Area works
conditions.text: All works within Root Protection Areas shall be undertaken under the supervision of a suitably qualified arboricultural consultant. A schedule of supervision visits and associated reports shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. To ensure adequate protection of retained trees.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination discovery and remediation
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site.

conditions.summary: Testing and approval of imported soil and soil-forming materials
conditions.text: Any soil or soil forming materials brought to site for use in garden areas, soft landscaping, public open space or for filling and level raising shall be tested for contamination and suitability for use. A methodology for testing these soils shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to these materials being imported onto site. The methodology shall include information on the source of the materials, sampling frequency, testing schedules and criteria against which the analytical results will be assessed (as determined by risk assessment).

conditions.summary: National Gas Asset Protection Plan approval
conditions.text: No development shall commence until a National Gas Asset Protection Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, in consultation with National Gas Transmission. The National Gas Asset Protection Plan shall include an Earthing Study, Lightning Strike Risk Assessment and reenergisation survey. The construction and operation of the site shall be carried out only in accordance with the approved National Gas Asset Protection Plan.

conditions.summary: Post-energisation survey of cathodic protection system
conditions.text: Within 3 months of being brought into use, a post energisation survey to assess the effects of the energisation on the pipeline's cathodic protection system should be carried out and the results submitted in a report to the local planning authority to be approved in consultation with NGT. The report should set out any mitigation measures if required to make the impact acceptable to NGT, and the scheme should be constructed and operated in accordance with those mitigation measure

conditions.summary: Battery Storage Safety Management Plan for transportation
conditions.text: Prior to commencement of development, a Battery Storage Safety Management Plan relating to the transportation of battery storage equipment along the Strategic Road Network shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with National Highways. In the interests of highway safety and network resilience.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Gain Plan submission and approval
conditions.text: The effect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 is that planning permission granted for development of land in England is deemed to have been granted subject to the condition (biodiversity gain condition) that development may not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority; and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. The planning authority, for the purposes of determining whether to approve a Biodiversity Gain Plan, if one is required in respect of this permission would be Leeds City Council.

On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that no unexpected significant contamination is encountered, written confirmation shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.

The methodology shall include information on the source of the materials, sampling frequency, testing schedules and criteria against which the analytical results will be assessed (as determined by risk assessment). Testing shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology. Relevant evidence, assessment and verification information shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the site or phase of the site being brought into use.

conditions.text: No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a) A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action b) A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action in the event that dust is identified as an issue or any complaints are received c) Details of a chassis and wheel cleaning system to be used for all construction vehicles leaving the site... d) Haul routes to the site and hours of delivery e) Measures to ensure that vehicles entering the site can do so immediately upon arrival. f) Details to ensure that any parking, waiting, loading/unloading only occurs in the marked out parking bay directly adjacent to the site... g) Details of any events that is likely to require a banksman for larger vehicles to reverse in to the site and methodology... h) Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning i) Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security j) Confirmation that any demolition will be carried out in accordance with the ecological assessment k) Details of site notice with contact details and a scheme for dealing with complaints l) Details of any temporary lighting which must not directly light the public highway m) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from the demolition and construction works n) The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate.

applications.address: Land To The South Of Pilton Village Luffenham Lane Pilton Rutland
applications.description: Full Planning Application for the installation and operation of a solar farm together with all associated works, equipment, necessary infrastructure and biodiversity enhancement areas.

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans and documents
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the details shown in the following approved documents and plans: [List of detailed plans and documents as specified]

conditions.summary: Finish and colour of structures and equipment
conditions.text: Notwithstanding any details submitted, no development shall commence on site until full details of the finish and colour of all structures, equipment, fencing and support frames for the solar panels hereby approved have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained thereafter for the lifetime of the development hereby approved.

conditions.summary: 40-year operational period and decommissioning requirements
conditions.text: Within 1 month of the date of first export of electricity to either the National Grid or to the Wing Water Treatment Works the use of the land for the generation of electricity as hereby permitted shall cease on or before the expiry of a 40-year period from the date of first export. The land shall thereafter be restored to its former condition in accordance with a scheme of decommissioning work.

conditions.summary: Tree and hedgerow protection during construction and decommissioning
conditions.text: Before any works commence on site other than site preparation works, the trees and hedgerows shown for retention on Plan BHA_4736_02 shall be protected as required in accordance with BS5837 and that plan and shall remain so protected until all construction on site is complete. The trees shall be protected during the decommissioning of the site in the same manner or in accordance with any standard that subsequently supersedes BS5837.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation and maintenance
conditions.text: All changes in hard landscaping, planting, seeding or turfing shown on the approved landscaping details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding season (October - March inclusive) following the commencement of the development or in such other phased arrangement as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years of being planted die are removed or seriously damaged or seriously diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.

conditions.summary: Noise impact assessment in accordance with BS4142:2014+A1(2019)
conditions.text: A noise impact assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The assessment shall be undertaken in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1(2019) prior to commencement, taking into account both day and night-time noise levels, and will be used to inform any necessary noise mitigation scheme for the proposed development. Thereafter the development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details, including any necessary mitigation, prior to first use, and shall thereafter be retained and maintained as such in perpetuity.

conditions.summary: Land contamination investigation and remediation scheme
conditions.text: No development other than that required to be carried out as part of an approved scheme of remediation shall commence until sections (i) to (iii) of this condition have been complied with. [Detailed requirements for site characterisation, submission of remediation scheme, implementation and reporting of unexpected contamination]

conditions.summary: Soil Management Plan for construction, operation and decommissioning
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of each phase of development (Construction, Operation and Decommissioning), a Soil Management Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include details pertaining to careful soil management during each phase, including consideration of the appropriate time of year for soil handling, planting beneath the panels and returning the land to the former land quality as indicated in Appendix 6 of the Agricultural Land Classification survey.

conditions.summary: Implementation of access arrangements on Morcott Road
conditions.text: Prior to the installation of the solar panel infrastructure for each phase the related access on Morcott Road shall be fully implemented in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1.

conditions.summary: Internal access roads, parking and turning facilities
conditions.text: Prior to commissioning the solar farm infrastructure, the facilities for internal access roads, parking and turning shall be fully implemented, with full details to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing prior to commencement. Following any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme, any damaged areas or routes will be fully remediated.

conditions.summary: Vehicle visibility splays at access points
conditions.text: Prior to commencement of development vehicle to vehicle visibility splays will be provided in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan, ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1, with no obstruction above 600mm above ground level and thereafter maintained until the completion of decommissioning the site.

conditions.summary: Construction vehicle routing via green route only
conditions.text: All construction vehicles associated with the solar panel areas and access via Morcott Road will use the green construction route only as shown on the Construction Traffic Routing Plan, ref P22-1447 Figure 4.1, which applies to the construction, any wholesale replacement scheme and decommissioning.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan requirements
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include: (a) noise and vibration monitoring scheme with hours of working; (b) dust control scheme; (c) wheel cleaning for construction vehicles; (d) vehicle access measures; (e) site compounds and parking; (f) site enclosure and security; (g) tree protection measures; (h) site notice and complaints procedure; (i) temporary lighting details; (j) phasing plans; (k) waste recycling/disposal; (l) security hoarding and public viewing facilities.

conditions.summary: Temporary parking and turning during construction and decommissioning
conditions.text: Temporary facilities for the internal access roads, parking, turning, loading and unloading of all vehicles visiting the site during the construction period shall be provided prior to installation of any solar panel infrastructure, prior to any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme and prior to the decommissioning period, in accordance with the details approved as part of the Construction Management Plan.

conditions.summary: Control of private temporary or permanent lighting
conditions.text: Any private temporary or permanent lighting shall be arranged so that no danger or inconvenience is caused to users of the public highway.

conditions.summary: Photographic survey of highways before and after construction
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of any work on the site, a photographic survey will be carried out of The Cock Pit, Back Lane, Wing Road and Morcott Road and submitted to the Local Planning Authority. A replica photographic survey will be carried out within one month of the completion of construction to identify any damage to the highway resulting from traffic movements associated with the development. Any identified damage will need to be remediated by the applicant within three months of the date of that survey.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan implementation
conditions.text: The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated May 2024) the updated Appendix 2 section 7, submitted to the Local Planning Authority on 11th July 2024, the Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated 1st May 2024) and Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (prepared by Pegasus Group, dated 1st February 2024).

conditions.summary: Construction surface water drainage management
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the construction stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed.

conditions.summary: Secondary surface water drainage for wholesale panel replacement
conditions.text: No wholesale replacement shall take place until a Secondary Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the construction stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed.

conditions.summary: Decommissioning surface water drainage management
conditions.text: No decommissioning shall take place until a Decommissioning Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the decommissioning stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for all phases, the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed.

conditions.summary: Construction hours limitation
conditions.text: Construction times (including deliveries) shall be limited to the following hours: 08:00 - 20:00 Monday to Friday; and 08:00 - 13:00 Saturdays. No construction works shall take place at any time on Sunday or a Bank Holidays. No works nor delivers shall take place outside of these time without the prior written agreement of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Cable route tree root protection areas
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the details approved as set out in condition 2 of this decision, prior to commencement of the works comprising the cable route from the solar site to the Oakham substation, detailed plans shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for its written approval of any section of the route not proposed to be within the confines of the public highway carriageway. These plans shall identify the root protection areas of any trees impacted on by the proposed cable route, alongside details of how the connection is to be made without resulting in damage to tree roots in those areas.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan approval required
conditions.text: No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a. A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action. b. A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action in the event that dust is identified as an issue or any complaints are received. c. Haul routes to the site from the strategic road network and hours of delivery d. Measures to ensure that vehicles can access the site immediately upon arrival to ensure there is no park, waiting, loading/unloading or queuing on the public highway. e. Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning. f. Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security. g. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.

conditions.summary: 30 year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan for biodiversity gain
conditions.text: The development shall not commence until a 30 year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan (HMMP), prepared in accordance with an approved Biodiversity Gain Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved HMMP shall be strictly adhered to and implemented in full for its duration and shall contain the following: a) Description and evaluation of the features to be managed; b) Ecological trends and constraints on site that may influence management; c) Aims, objectives and targets for management - links with local and national species and habitat action plans; d) Description of the management operations necessary to achieving aims and objectives; e) Preparation of a works schedule, including annual works schedule; f) Details and a timetable of the monitoring needed to measure the effectiveness of management; g) Details of the persons responsible for the implementation and monitoring; h) Mechanisms of adaptive management to account for necessary changes in work schedule to achieve the required targets; and i) Details of methodology and frequency of monitoring reports to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority to assess biodiversity gain

conditions.summary: Public Right of Way Operational Safety Plan approval required
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation or use of the development, a Public Right of Way (PROW) Operational Safety Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include: An assessment of the operational phase risks to users of Public Footpath E227 arising from vehicle and pedestrian movements within the site following completion of the development; Details of the permanent measures to manage pedestrian/vehicle interaction, including routing, surface markings, lining, signage and visibility improvements; Arrangements for the future monitoring, maintenance and upgrading of the measures where required to ensure continued safe operation for the lifetime of the development. The development shall thereafter operate only in accordance with the approved PROW Operational Safety Plan.

conditions.text:
i. No advertisement is to be displayed without the permission of the owner of the site or any other person with an interest in the site entitled to grant permission.
ii. No advertisement shall be sited or displayed so as to:
a. endanger persons using any highway, railway, waterway, dock, harbour or aerodrome (civil or military);
b. obscure, or hinder the ready interpretation of, any traffic sign, railway signal or aid to navigation by water or air; or
c. hinder the operation of any device used for the purpose of security or surveillance or for measuring the speed of any vehicle.
iii. Any advertisement displayed, and any site used for the display of advertisements, shall be maintained in a condition that does not impair the visual amenity of the site.
iv. Any structure or hoarding erected or used principally for the purpose of displaying advertisements shall be maintained in a condition that does not endanger the public.

conditions.summary: Site contamination assessment, remediation and validation
conditions.text: Site Characterisation: No development shall take place until an assessment of the nature and extent of contamination has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, undertaken by a competent person as defined by annex 2 of the National Planning Framework. The assessment must include a survey of extent, scale and nature of contamination and develop the conceptual site model to assess and evaluate potential risks to human health, property, adjoining land, groundwaters and surface waters, ecological systems, archaeological sites and ancient monuments, conducted in accordance with the Environment Agency's 'Land Contamination Risk Management' Guidance. Submission of Remediation Scheme: No development shall take place until a detailed remediation scheme to bring the site to a condition suitable for the intended use has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme must include all works to be undertaken, proposed remediation objectives and criteria, an appraisal of remedial options, and timetable of works and site management procedures. Implementation of Approved Remediation Scheme: The remediation scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved timetable of works. Within 3 months of completion, a validation report must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. Reporting of Unexpected Contamination: In the event that contamination is found when carrying out the approved development that was not previously identified, it must be reported in writing within 5 days to the Local Planning Authority and development must be halted on that part of the site.

conditions.text: Within 1 month of the date of first export of electricity to either the National Grid or to the Wing Water Treatment Works ("the date of first export") confirmation shall be provided in writing to the Local Planning Authority of the same. The use of the land for the generation of electricity as hereby permitted shall cease on or before the expiry of a 40-year period from the date of first export. The land shall thereafter be restored to its former condition in accordance with a scheme of decommissioning work ("Decommissioning Method Statement"). The Decommissioning Method Statement, including the dismantling and removal of all elements (with the exception of the Substation and associated access), shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval not later than 39 years and 6 months from the date of first export of electricity, or within 3 months of the cessation of electricity generation at the site, whichever is earlier. The approved scheme shall be carried out and completed within 6 months from the date that the planning permission hereby granted expires.

conditions.summary: Tree and hedgerow protection during construction and decommissioning
conditions.text: Before any works commence on site other than site preparation works, the trees and hedgerows shown for retention on Plan BHA_4736_02 shall be protected as required in accordance with BS5837 and that plan and shall remain so protected until all construction on site is complete. The trees shall be protected during the decommissioning of the site in the same manner or in accordance with any standard that subsequently supersedes BS5837.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation and maintenance
conditions.text: All changes in hard landscaping, planting, seeding or turfing shown on the approved landscaping details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding season (October - March inclusive) following the commencement of the development or in such other phased arrangement as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years of being planted die are removed or seriously damaged or seriously diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.

conditions.summary: Noise impact assessment and mitigation compliance
conditions.text: The development shall be implemented in accordance with the noise impact assessment provided and approved under application reference 2025/1257/DIS, including any necessary mitigation, prior to its first use, and shall thereafter be retained and maintained in accordance with those details in perpetuity.

conditions.summary: Contamination investigation and remediation
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations of the investigation reports submitted under application 2026/0225/DIS. In the event that contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved development that was not previously identified it shall be reported in writing within 5 days to the Local Planning Authority and once the Local Planning Authority has identified the part of the site affected by the unexpected contamination development must be halted on that part of the site. An investigation and risk assessment shall be undertaken in accordance with specifications to be provided by the local planning authority in line with the requirements of part (i) of condition 8 of permission 2024/0300/MAF, and where remediation is necessary a remediation scheme shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of section (ii) of that condition, which shall be approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Following completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme a verification report shall be prepared and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with section (iii) of the aforementioned condition.

conditions.summary: Soil management plan for construction, operations and decommissioning
conditions.text: Part a - construction and operations: The development shall be implemented and operated in accordance with the Soil Management Plan approved under application 2025/0497/DIS. Part b - decommissioning: Prior to the decommissioning of the development, a Soil Management Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include, but not be limited to details pertaining to careful soil management during each phase, including consideration of the appropriate time of year for soil handling, planting beneath the panels and returning the land to the former land quality as indicated in Appendix 6 of the Agricultural Land Classification survey dated 3rd March 2023 - Issue 4 carried out by Amet Property.

conditions.summary: Access implementation on Morcott Road
conditions.text: Prior to the installation of the solar panel infrastructure for each phase the related access on Morcott Road shall be fully implemented in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1.

conditions.summary: Internal access roads, parking and turning provision
conditions.text: Prior to commissioning the solar farm infrastructure, the facilities for internal access roads, parking and turning shall be fully implemented in accordance with the details submitted within the Construction Management Plan (ref: P22-1447 TR04 Rev E). Following any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme, any damaged areas or routes will be fully remediated.

conditions.summary: Vehicle visibility splays at access points
conditions.text: Prior to commencement of development vehicle to vehicle visibility splays will be provided in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan, ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1 of the Construction Management Plan (ref: P22-1447 TR04 Rev E), with no obstruction above 600mm above ground level. The visibility splays shall be thereafter maintained until the completion of decommissioning the site.

conditions.summary: Construction vehicle routing and access for replacement and decommissioning
conditions.text: All construction vehicles associated with the solar panel areas and access via Morcott Road shall use the construction route approved under the terms of application reference 2025/1123/FUL. No wholesale replacement of solar panels or decommissioning works shall take place at the site until details of the proposed access route for those works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details shall be submitted not less than three months prior to the commencement of the relevant wholesale replacement or decommissioning works, and shall include the proposed route, any temporary access arrangements, measures for managing construction traffic, and any mitigation required in the interests of highway safety. The wholesale replacement or decommissioning works shall thereafter be carried out only in accordance with the approved access route and associated details. In the event that no alternative access route is approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, such works shall be carried out using the green construction route shown on the Construction Traffic Routing Plan, reference P22-1447 Figure 4.1 approved under application reference 2024/0300/MAF.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan compliance
conditions.text: The development hereby approved, shall be carried out in strict accordance with the Construction Management Plan Revision E dated July 2026.

conditions.summary: Temporary facilities for construction, replacement and decommissioning
conditions.text: Temporary facilities for the internal access roads, parking, turning, loading and unloading of all vehicles visiting the site during the construction period shall be provided prior to installation of any solar panel infrastructure, prior to any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme and prior to the decommissioning period, in accordance with the details approved as part of the Construction Management Plan.

conditions.summary: Private temporary or permanent lighting control
conditions.text: Any private temporary or permanent lighting shall be arranged so that no danger or inconvenience is caused to users of the public highway.

conditions.summary: Pre and post-construction photographic highway surveys
conditions.text: A pre-commencement photographic survey has been carried out of The Cock Pit, Back Lane (between The Cock Pit and Wing Road), Wing Road (between Back Lane and Morcott Road), and Morcott Road (between Wing Road and 50m north of Pinfold Lane) and submitted to the Local Planning Authority. A replica photographic survey shall be carried out within one month of the completion of construction to identify any damage to the highway resulting from traffic movements associated with the development and submitted to the Local Planning Authority. Any identified damage will need to be remediated by the applicant within three months of the date of that survey. Pre-construction and post-construction surveys of the same locations will also be required for any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme and for the decommissioning stage.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity enhancement, management and net gain compliance
conditions.text: The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated May 2024) the updated Appendix 2 section 7, submitted to the Local Planning Authority on 11th July 2024, the Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated 1st May 2024) and Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (prepared by Pegasus Group, dated 1st February 2024).

conditions.summary: Construction Method Statement compliance for drainage
conditions.text: The Construction Method Statement approved under application 2025/0584/DIS shall be strictly adhered to throughout the construction period.

conditions.summary: Secondary Construction Method Statement for wholesale replacement
conditions.text: No wholesale replacement shall take place until a Secondary Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the construction stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed. The approved Secondary Construction Method Statement shall thereafter be strictly adhered to throughout the wholesale replacement period.

conditions.summary: Decommissioning Method Statement for drainage control
conditions.text: No decommissioning shall take place until a Decommissioning Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the decommissioning stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for all phases, the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed. The approved Decommissioning Method Statement shall thereafter be strictly adhered to throughout the decommissioning period.

conditions.summary: Construction hours and delivery times
conditions.text: Construction times (including deliveries) shall be limited to the following hours: 08:00 - 20:00 Monday to Friday; and 08:00 - 13:00 Saturdays. No construction works shall take place at any time on Sunday or a Bank Holidays. No works nor deliveries shall take place outside of these times without the prior written agreement of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Cable route tree root protection details
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the details approved as set out in condition 2 of this decision, prior to commencement of the works comprising the cable route from the solar site to the Oakham substation, detailed plans shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for its written approval of any section of the route not proposed to be within the confines of the public highway carriageway. These plans shall identify the root protection areas of any trees impacted on by the proposed cable route, alongside details of how the connection is to be made without resulting in damage to tree roots in those areas. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.text: No development shall commence until details of existing pub garden and proposed terrace levels of the site, finished floor levels and identifying all areas of cut or fill, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be completed in accordance with the agreed scheme before the extension and terrace are first used.

conditions.summary: Bat Roost Assessment mitigation measures compliance

conditions.summary: Accordance with approved plans

conditions.summary: Commencement of development within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: External materials specification
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be completed in accordance with the external materials specified within drawing number 7744-08-430 REV 6 as approved or any alternatives to be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Hard and soft landscaping implementation
conditions.text: All hard and soft landscaping shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details as set out in drawing numbers 08-420 rev 6 and TRP1 rev 2 to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant British Standards or other recognised Codes of Good Practice.

conditions.summary: Planting, seeding or turfing completion timing
conditions.text: All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner.

conditions.summary: Retained tree protection (five years)
conditions.text: No tree shown retained on the approved plans shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be topped or lopped within five years of the completion of development without the written approval of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Replacement tree planting
conditions.text: If any retained tree referred to in condition 6 is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies within 5 years of the completion of development, a replacement tree should be planted in the same place and that tree shall be of such a size and species, and shall be planted at such time, as may be specified in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Tree protection fencing (BS5837:2012)
conditions.text: Before any development commences, including any site clearance or demolition works, any trees on the site to be retained shall be protected by fencing or other means of enclosure in accordance with BS5837:2012.

conditions.summary: Bird nesting season vegetation clearance
conditions.text: All areas of hedges, scrub or similar vegetation where birds may nest which are to be removed as part of the development, are to be cleared outside the bird-nesting season (March - August inclusive) or if clearance during the bird nesting season cannot be reasonably be avoided, a suitably qualified ecologist will check the areas to be removed immediately prior to clearance and advise whether nesting birds are present. If active nests are recorded, no vegetation clearance or other works that may disturb active nests shall proceed until all young have fledged the nest.

conditions.summary: Habitat management and biodiversity net gain implementation
conditions.text: The recommended habitat management and ecological enhancements set out within the Ecological Assessment and Biodiversity Net Gain Plan by EPR dated August 2023 ref. 22/86-3B shall be implemented and permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 23069-0000-P1; 23069-0100-P1; 23069-0101-P1; ASC.23.521; 23069-0300-P1; 23069-1103-P2; 23069-1100-P3; 23069-1101-P2; 23069-1102-P2; 23069-1300-P4;

conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Construction hours and deliveries restriction
conditions.text: No demolition, construction or maintenance activities audible at the boundary, and no deliveries of construction and demolition materials shall be undertaken outside the hours 07:30 hours to 18:00 hours Monday to Friday and 08:00 hours to 13:00 hours on Saturdays. For the avoidance of doubt, no such activity shall take place on Sundays or Bank Holidays, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: External lighting to avoid spillage beyond site boundaries
conditions.text: Any external lighting installed at the site shall be angled so as to avoid any spillage beyond the site boundaries unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Contaminated land investigation and remediation
conditions.text: In the event that contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved development that was not previously identified, it must be reported in writing immediately to the local planning authority. An investigation and risk assessment must be undertaken and where remediation is necessary, a remediation scheme must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Following completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme, a verification report must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

conditions.summary: Replacement of dead or damaged landscape planting within five years
conditions.text: Any trees or plants comprised within the scheme of landscaping, which within a period of five years from the completion of the development die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Landscaping to be carried out in first planting season
conditions.text: All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the first occupation of the building(s) or the completion of the development whichever is the sooner.

conditions.summary: Noise Impact Assessment compliance
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the Noise Impact Assessment prepared by IEC Limited, reference IEC/4552/01/AVH dated 08.12.2023 and subsequent Technical Note reference IEC001 dated 01.08.2024 unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Ground floor units as Category 2 accessible and adaptable dwellings
conditions.text: The ground floor residential units should all be Category 2: Accessible and Adaptable dwellings.

conditions.summary: Minimum Finished Floor Level for flood resistance
conditions.text: The development will be constructed as per the approved documents including the minimum Finished Floor Level (FFL) of 90.9 mAOD. This is to ensure that the development should be appropriately flood resistant and resilient such that, in the event of a flood, it could be quickly brought back into use without significant refurbishment.

conditions.summary: Obscured glazing and opening restrictions to eastern windows
conditions.text: The first floor windows in the eastern side elevation of the development hereby approved shall be glazed with obscured glass and shall be fixed so as to be incapable of being opened below a height of 1.7 metres above floor level, and shall be retained in that form thereafter.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan required
conditions.text: No development shall commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Highway Authority. Thereafter the construction of the development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan. The Plan would need to include details of: a. Construction vehicle numbers, type, routing; b. Access arrangements to the site; c. Traffic management requirements; d. Construction and storage compounds (including areas designated for car parking); e. Siting and details of wheel washing facilities; f. Cleaning of site entrances, site tracks and the adjacent public highway; g. Timing of construction activities including delivery times and removal of waste, and to avoid school pick up/drop off times. h. Provision of sufficient on-site parking prior to commencement of construction activities; i. Post construction restoration/reinstatement of the working areas and temporary access to the public highway; j. where works cannot be contained wholly within the site a plan should be submitted showing the site layout on the highway including extent of hoarding, pedestrian routes and remaining road width for vehicle movements; k. Phasing Plan.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures required prior to commencement
conditions.text: No development shall take place (including site clearance and demolition) until details of tree protection measures for the trees to the south of the application site and any trees on the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The tree protection measures as approved shall be implemented prior to commencement of development and remain in place until the development has been completed. Within the tree protection areas to be fenced off there shall be no alteration to the ground level and they shall be kept clear of vehicles, materials, surplus soil, temporary buildings, plant and machinery.

conditions.summary: Site Waste Management Plan required
conditions.text: No development shall take place (including site clearance and demolition) until a Site Waste Management Plan (SWMP) for the site has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in consultation with the Waste Planning Authority. The SWMP should aim to reduce the amount of waste produced on site and should contain information including estimated types and quantities of waste to arise from construction and waste management actions for each waste type. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved SWMP.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage construction drawings and method statement
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, construction drawings of the surface water drainage network, associated sustainable drainage components and flow control mechanisms and a construction method statement shall be submitted and agreed in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall then be constructed as per the agreed drawings, method statement, Drainage Strategy and Drawings (Drainage Strategy and Drawing Rev P6, dated 15 December 2025) and remaining in perpetuity for the lifetime of the development unless agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No alteration to the agreed drainage scheme shall occur without prior written approval from the Local Authority.

conditions.summary: External materials schedule and samples approval
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until a schedule and samples of the materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Climate change adaptation measures
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of measures to address adaptation to climate change have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These measures shall then be implemented and permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Boundary treatment details approval
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of the treatment of all boundaries including details of any walls, fences, gates or other means of enclosure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of development. The approved boundary treatments shall be completed before the use hereby permitted is commenced or before the building(s) is occupied.

conditions.summary: Soft and hard landscaping scheme approval
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until there has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority a scheme of soft and hard landscaping and details of the treatment of all hard surfaces. The scheme shall include details of all existing trees and hedgerows on the land and details showing all trees to be removed, or retained, together with details of all new planting to take place including species, size and method of planting.

conditions.summary: Water supplies and fire hydrants scheme
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until a scheme for the provision of adequate water supplies and fire hydrants, necessary for firefighting purposes at the site, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be occupied until the scheme has been implemented in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Integrated swift bricks and bat boxes provision
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of integrated swift bricks and bat boxes to be provided within the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Parking provision and sustainable drainage implementation
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings herby permitted the parking provision as shown on the approved plans, shall be constructed, hardsurfaced and made ready for use. Any new areas of hardstanding created, or existing areas which are replaced, shall be constructed in a porous material or provision shall be made for a sustainable urban drainage system (SuDS) to be built into the hardsurfaced areas. Once provided the parking facilities shall be retained in that form and thereafter be used for the parking of vehicles only.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charging point infrastructure provision
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellinghouses hereby permitted, all parking spaces shall be provided with the underlying infrastructure for connection to the electricity network to enable them to be served by an electric vehicle charging point.

conditions.summary: Cycle storage provision and retention
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings hereby permitted, the cycle storage as shown on approved plan 23069-1100-P3, for the storage of not less than 20 cycles in a single storey formation shall be implemented accordingly. The cycle storage shall be retained and maintained accordingly during the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Waste and recycling storage area implementation
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings hereby permitted, the waste and recycling storage area as shown on plan 23069-1100-P3 shall be implemented accordingly. The storage shall be retained and maintained accordingly during the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Maintenance and management plan for sustainable drainage scheme
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until details of the maintenance and management of the sustainable drainage scheme have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The drainage scheme shall be implemented prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved and thereafter managed and maintained in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity. The Local Planning Authority shall be granted access to inspect the sustainable drainage scheme for the lifetime of the development. The details of the scheme to be submitted for approval shall include: i. a timetable for its implementation. ii. details of SuDS feature and connecting drainage structures and maintenance requirement for each aspect including a drawing showing where they are located. iii. a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development which shall include the arrangements for adoption by any public body or statutory undertaker, or any other arrangements to secure the operation of the sustainable drainage scheme throughout its lifetime. This will include the name and contact details of any appointed management company. Hertfordshire County Council

The survey and report shall demonstrate that the surface water drainage system has been constructed in accordance with the details approved pursuant to condition 15. Where necessary, details of corrective works to be carried out along with a timetable for their completion, shall be included for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any corrective works required shall be carried out in accordance with the approved timetable and subsequently re-surveyed with the findings submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The plan shall show the type and locations of external lighting, as well as the expected light spill in lux levels, to demonstrate that areas to be lit shall not adversely impact biodiversity. All external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the specifications and locations set out in the plan and shall be maintained thereafter.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Enhancement Plan with habitat and bat/bird boxes
conditions.text: Within six months of the date of this decision, a Biodiversity Enhancement Plan (BEP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Plan shall include full details of the biodiversity enhancements to be implemented on-site. The Plan shall include: A detailed, scaled soft landscaping plan, planting schedule and relevant habitat management measures; The enhancement of hedgerow habitat as shown on drawing As Existing Site Plan, dated February 2026, by WS Planning Architecture; Provision of one suitably placed bat and/or bird boxes, with the exact locations, make and model and height from ground level shown on scaled plans suitable for construction. In the case of building mounted boxes, scaled elevation plans shall be provided. Boxes for breeding birds shall be targeted at S41 priority species and/or red/amber listed species as listed within the latest British Trust for Ornithology Birds of Conservation Concern report. Boxes shall be building integrated and/or constructed of woodcrete to ensure durability. The Plan shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details during the next available planting season following its approval and all features shall be retained in that manner thereafter.
